A Tree Walk with Kavya Chandra, in collaboration with Bangalore Creative Circus and Climate Week India

What can the trees around us tell us about Bengaluru?

Through the lanes of Mahalakshmi Layout, we’ll get to rediscover the trees and plants that shape our everyday landscapes—their ecological roles, fascinating stories, origins, relationships with birds and insects, and the ways they have adapted to life in an ever-changing city.

We’ll also look at Bengaluru itself through the lens of its trees—how the city has grown, how its landscapes have changed, and how plants quietly tell stories of the city’s history, people, climate and culture.

Come walk, observe, listen and perhaps look at the trees you pass every day a little differently.

11.15am to 12.15pm, Sunday, 4th October
Price - 835 INR per head
Open to all ages 

Starting near Mahalakshmi Metro Station (Google Maps location will be shared) and ending at Bangalore Creative Circus, to experience the BCC Carnival - featuring conscious market stalls, workshops, activities, live performances, and lots of food!

Before anything changes, someone has to imagine that it could be different.

At the Festival of Defiance, the day moves through six themes: Imagination, Belonging, Taste, Action, Curiosity and Evidence.

We’re starting with Imagination.

Not imagination as an abstract idea, but as a way of asking:

Could we organise our communities differently?
Could we learn differently?
Could our economies, our relationship with nature, or even our idea of the future look different?

That’s the territory our Imagination Weavers are bringing into the festival.

Adil Basha works with alternative economies, community building and social experiments.

Deepika Manoharan works across sustainability, alternative futures and internet culture.

Ashik Krishnan works with experiential learning, alternative futures and youth networks.

They’re not coming to talk about imagination. They’re creating spaces where you can use it.

Festival of Defiance
10 October, 10 AM–6 PM
at Bangalore Creative Circus,
Yeshwantpur 

Register at bit.ly/DEFYNOW
Visit https://fod.projectdefy.org/ to know more about the festival.

Kintsugi is the Japanese practice of repairing broken pottery with gold. Instead of hiding the crack, you highlight it, and the piece ends up more interesting than it was before it broke.

We use it as an art therapy process. You’ll get your own ceramic piece, break it, and spend the morning putting it back together and finishing the seams in gold. Alongside the making, there’s guided journaling and space to talk, so you’re reflecting as you work rather than just doing a craft activity. The session is designed and led by psychologists, so the room is properly held.

No artistic ability needed. Genuinely none. Most people arrive slightly unsure and leave not wanting to go.

What’s included:
A ceramic piece to break, mend and take home, all kintsugi materials, guided art therapy through the session, and a reflective journal that’s yours to keep. Food can be ordered from thecircuscanteen at the venue.

10:00 AM to 1:30 PM
at Bangalore Creative Circus, Yeshwantpur

You’ve defied something. A job you left, a life you chose differently, an expectation you refused. It’s usually a lonely business.

On 10th October 2026, it isn’t.

Welcome to the Festival of Defiance, where defiants gather. Those who chose to build their own path.
 
What happens?
Conversations. Films. Immersive experiences. Building things from scratch. Exhibitions. A human library. Healing circles and journaling. Music. Stories. Play. Quiet corners. Chai, all day.
 
Who’s leading it?
People and collectives from across the country who have already defied something and built the alternative. 
 
Who’s it for?
Anyone questioning, building, learning or living a little differently. And anyone who wants to, but hasn’t started.
 
What do you leave with?
A community of defiants. People who have defied norms. Inspiration, intention, and a first action.
 
Where and when? 
Bangalore Creative Circus, Saturday 10 October, 10 AM - 6 PM
 
This is your community. Come and find it.
 
Link in bio to register

Most of us don’t struggle only with the big decisions.

Sometimes it’s the quieter ones.

The choice you’ve been going back and forth on.
The conversation you’re not sure how to have.
The next step you keep wondering about.
Something you know matters, but haven’t quite found clarity around.

Sometimes, we don’t need someone to tell us what to do.
We need a little space to slow down and see what we’ve been sitting with a little differently.

The Art of Gentle Choices is an intimate Flow Game circle where you can bring what you’ve been sitting with and explore it through reflection, conversation and unexpected perspectives.

You don’t need to have anything figured out.
You don’t need prior experience with reflective spaces.

Just come as you are, and bring what you’ve been sitting with.

You may leave with a little more clarity than you came with.
A different way of seeing things.
Perhaps a gentle next step that feels right for you.

No advance fee. 
Experience the circle first.

Choose what’s comfortable to contribute at the end of th circle

Sunday, September 13th, 2026
10:45 AM – 1:00 PM
at Bangalore Creative Circus, Yeshwantpur

It’s a simple but powerful guided experience.

You bring a question around a choice you have been sitting with. 
The circle helps you explore it, through reflection, conversation, and unexpected insights.

If something has been on your mind lately, perhaps this is a space to bring it.

We’re reserving spots through a WhatsApp group. Link in bio to join

A little under a week out from The Working Woman’s Hormone Toolkit’s first Bangalore session.

It’s a small room by design. Two hours, one topic — hormonal cycles — and enough space to actually work through it, not just sit through a talk. 

The session is science-backed but built for beginners; no prior knowledge needed, just curiosity about your own body. By the end, participants walk away with a fundamental understanding of female biology, clarity on their own hormonal state, and a personal action plan they can start using immediately. Not more open tabs to figure out later.

It’s facilitated by Aditi Singhal, a certified holistic health & nutrition specialist with a research background in gut health, who has run such workshops for 300+ participants across the US, Canada, and Mexico. This is the first time it’s happening in India.

📍 Bangalore Creative Circus, Yeshwantpur
🗓️ 12th September, 2026 | 11 AM–1 PM

The Working Woman’s Hormone Toolkit is finally coming to Bangalore, debuting at Bangalore Creative Circus on 12th September. It is a science-backed, 2-hour intensive on understanding your hormonal cycles and working with your biology, not against it, at work and in life.

Facilitated by Aditi Singhal, a certified holistic health & nutrition specialist, with an academic research background in gut health. Having personally navigated the gap between Western health science, traditional approaches, and the realities of being an Indian woman in a western healthcare system, she built this workshop to leave women feeling informed and empowered, not stuck cycling through symptoms and a dissapointing healthcare system. She has conducted 200+ such workshops across the US, Canada, and Mexico, and this marks her first time bringing one to Bangalore.

In 2 hours, you’ll walk away with:
— a fundamental understanding of female biology
— clarity on your own hormonal state
— a personal action plan you can start using immediately

📍 Bangalore Creative Circus, Yeshwantpur
12th September, 2026 | 11 AM–1 PM
